name: Kwato
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog lists only classificatory references (Pawley 2005; Pawley & Hammarstrom 2017); no grammar or phonology of Kwato located.

sources.citation: SIL Language & Culture Archives listing for [kop] (the Internet Archive 2024) and OLAC combined catalogue for kop (the Internet Archive 2024)
sources.note: Catalogue records only: SIL lists a single item (the 2009 survey report); OLAC lists the two SIL wordlists (Priestley 1979, Kassell 2003), Rosetta Swadesh list, transnewguinea.org entry (source Z'graggen 1980), PARADISEC DWU story recordings, and Glottolog. No grammar, phonology or Organised Phonology Data exists for Waube.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2010. Change Request 2010-029: [kop] Kwato > Waube (adopted 2011-05-18).
sources.note: Nothing; name change only, cites Tucker et al. 2009 (SILESR 2009-017) as its sole source.

sources.citation: Lambrecht, Philip, Alison Kassell, Margaret Potter & Sarah Tucker. 2009. The sociolinguistic profile of the Waube [kop] language. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2009-017. 47 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. §6.1 'Characteristics of the Language' (p. 24) gives only consonant/vowel phone tables (Tables 6.1–6.2), free variation of voiced/voiceless stops, and SOV order; Appendix F wordlists (pp. 41–46) carry no stress marks.

sources.citation: Kassell, Alison. 2003. Kwato Wordlist, Madang Province, 2003. SIL International, Ukarumpa (OLAC oai:sil.org:67610).
sources.note: Nine-village 190-item survey wordlist; the original elicitation sheets may carry stress ticks like Priestley 1979; the archive page links only to the 1979 file.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1980. A comparative word list of the Rai Coast languages, Madang Province, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics D-30. Canberra: ANU. (Kwato = list B21)
sources.note: Nothing. Introduction §7 (pp. vii–ix): transcription 'semiphonemic'; fluctuation table gives Kwato d ~ r, z ~ y; vowel length marked with a colon in the Kwato column; no stress marks and no occurrence of 'stress'/'accent' in the text.

sources.citation: Priestley, Ian. 1979. Kwato [kop] word list, Madang Province. SIL Survey Word List (Standard), handwritten, language 'Waupe', village Paraiye, elicited 22 Oct 1979. Ukarumpa: SIL. 12 pp. (OLAC oai:sil.org:67609)
sources.note: No statement. Handwritten phonetic forms carry a primary-stress tick on many items, nearly all word-initial ('mamu 'dog', 'jaberemana 'he sits', 'inita 'he lies down', 'agemana 'he walks', 'jaro 'road', 'nɛniba 'stone', 'aro 'big', 'ɛpi 'fire', 'agerau 'ear', 'ɛmɛ 'breast'); raw data only, no rule stated.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, Johannes A. 1975. The Madang-Adelbert Range Sub-Phylum. In Wurm (ed.), New Guinea Area Languages and Language Study Vol 1, 569–612. Pacific Linguistics C-38.
sources.note: Nothing; Kwato (B21) appears only in cognate tables; no 'stress'/'accent' in text.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, John A. 1975. The languages of the Madang District, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics B-41.
Z'graggen, J. A. 1971. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Madang District. Pacific Linguistics C-19.
sources.note: Nothing on stress; §2.21.5 phonological typology of the Madang Phylum concerns segment inventories only; Kwato appears only in the name index ('Kwato KWA, Astrolabe Bay').

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page kwat1244; Wikipedia 'Waube language'; transnewguinea.org/language/waube; archive.org rosettaproject_kop_swadesh-1
sources.note: Nothing. Glottolog cites only Pawley 2005, Pawley & Hammarström 2017 (classification) and Ethnologue; Wikipedia is a stub citing Ethnologue; transnewguinea.org names Z'graggen 1980 as sole source with no prosodic notes.

sources.citation: Anonymous. n.d. Ramu Wordlists: Includes Kou, Kobuka, Wabe & Usino Languages. 9 pp. (Glottolog ref 568321)

sources.note: Only other Glottolog-listed primary data on Waube ('Wabe'); a phonetic wordlist that could carry stress marks.
